diversity_clusters_at_floor_0.55.caveat: This embedding-cosine metric answers a different question from atlas_only.distinct_louvain_clusters_covered below, and the two can legitimately disagree (e.g. both near 1). Every candidate here was retrieved *because* it matched the query topically, so abstract embeddings for both sets tend to clump into one semantic cluster regardless of which 25 (or 15) got picked — that's expected, not a bug. Louvain over the citation graph clusters by *citation structure* instead, which has nothing to do with abstract-text similarity and is the metric that actually speaks to breadth the loop can find and one-shot cosine ranking cannot.

citation_breadth.note: clusters_covered counts only papers with at least one OpenAlex reference (a paper with none would be its own singleton cluster and inflate breadth); compare papers_with_references too. Same graph, same clustering for both sets.
